title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
gist: Merck and Moderna said their personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine intismeran (mRNA-4157), combined with Keytruda, cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42 percent versus Keytruda plus placebo in a 1,137-patient Phase 3 trial of resected stage IIB-IV melanoma. The companies are already talking with regulators about approval. The effect was weaker than in the five-year Phase 2 trial (49 percent).

insights.claim: In a Phase 3 trial, Moderna and Merck's personalized mRNA vaccine intismeran (mRNA-4157) combined with Keytruda cut the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42 percent compared with Keytruda plus placebo. After two years, 82 percent of the combination group were alive without recurrence, against 70 percent of the Keytruda-placebo group.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: This is a positive pivotal readout for MRNA and MRK, which strengthens the case for an approval filing and a new revenue line from an individualized cancer vaccine.

insights.claim: Intismeran plus Keytruda reduced the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38 percent versus Keytruda plus placebo in the Phase 3 melanoma trial, with 88.5 percent versus 80 percent of patients alive without distant metastasis at the end of the trial.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The benefit on a second endpoint supports the label case and how the drug may be used in the adjuvant setting.

insights.claim: The Phase 3 trial enrolled 1,137 patients with surgically removed stage IIB-IV melanoma and randomized them 2-1 to the personalized mRNA vaccine plus Keytruda or to Keytruda alone.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Gives the trial size and population, which define the likely first-approval indication.

insights.claim: The Phase 3 treatment effect of intismeran was weaker than in the five-year Phase 2 trial, which showed a 49 percent reduction in the risk of recurrence or death and a 59 percent reduction in the risk of distant metastasis or death.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Effect sizes shrank from Phase 2 to Phase 3, which may temper peak-sales expectations built on the Phase 2 data.

insights.claim: Intismeran uses synthetic mRNA that encodes up to 34 mutations found in a patient's own cancer cells. Each vaccine is made by comparing the genetic sequences of the tumor with those of healthy cells and picking cancer-specific mutations so the immune response targets only the cancer.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Making a vaccine per patient requires sequencing and bespoke production, which brings manufacturing and logistics hurdles alongside a defensible platform moat.
insights.quote: holds the unique genetic coding for up to 34 mutations in a patient’s own cancer cells

insights.claim: Merck and Moderna are already engaging with regulatory authorities to get the personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine approved. The full data has been accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A near-term regulatory filing is a catalyst to watch for both companies.

insights.claim: Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said the results reinforce Moderna's conviction that mRNA could fundamentally change how cancer is treated, using treatments matched to each patient's tumor.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Moderna is presenting oncology as the post-COVID growth story for its mRNA platform.

insights.claim: Dean Li, president of Merck Research Laboratories, called the trial the first Phase 3 study to show a clinically meaningful improvement in recurrence-free and distant metastasis-free survival over standard-of-care Keytruda in resected melanoma, and one of the most significant advances in melanoma treatment since immunotherapy.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A combination with Keytruda could extend Merck's franchise in the adjuvant setting.
